lesson_title: What One Vetkoek Costs: Manufacturing and Cost Calculations
hook_text: She sells at R4. They cost R4,50 to make. She thinks she's winning.
clip_script: Your aunt takes a wedding order: four hundred vetkoek. Flour and oil — R2 inside each one. The cousin who fries — R1 per unit. That's R3 each, R1 200 for the order: the prime cost. But the kitchen itself costs money: the gas bottle, the wear on her big pots, the neighbour watching the stove — R600 that belongs to ALL the vetkoek and none in particular. The overheads. Total: R1 800. Divide by four hundred: R4,50. THAT number is the floor under her price. Sell at R6 — every unit clears R1,50. But price at R4 because a competitor did? Every single vetkoek now sells at a 50-cent loss that FEELS like business — money moving, customers happy — while it quietly eats her savings. A maker who doesn't know the unit cost isn't pricing. She's guessing. And the kitchen rent doesn't care how busy she is — which is exactly why she must.
visual_style: A warm township kitchen: costs sorting themselves into glowing bins above the pots (inside-each-one vs keeps-the-kitchen-cooking), stacking into three layers, dividing into a floor line under a price tag that dips below it and flashes red.
mood: Warm, personal, with a sharp protective edge — family business wisdom.
pacing: Cosy build through the layers, hard stop on the R4 price trap, empowering close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the floor under any price.
